newsitem.title: INDIA: India Chidambaram defends tax amnesty with warning.
newsitem.headline: India Chidambaram defends tax amnesty with warning.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Friday defended an amnesty scheme he offered to tax evaders in his budget this year, but said authorities would crack down on tax dodgers in the future.

"We must give a chance to people to come clean," Chidambaram told parliament in his reply to a debate on the Finance Bill containing tax and tariff proposals in the budget for 1997/98 (April-March), adding it was the "last chance".

"We have tightened up seizure procedures. Behind the velvet glove, there is a firm fist. I will not hesitate to prosecute those who violate income-tax laws after the new taxes are approved by the house," Chidambaram said.

Chidambaram presented the budget that proposed cuts in import duties, as well as personal and corporate tax rates on February 28. He told parliament that he expected compliance to increase following the tax cuts.

Debate on the Finance Bill began on Wednesday and a vote in the lower house, Lok Sabha, was set for after 2 p.m. (0830 GMT) on Friday. The upper house, Rajya Sabha, was expected to adopt the bill next week.
The Lok Sabha approved the appropriations bill containing the budget's spending proposals on Tuesday.
Chidambaram's Voluntary Disclosure of Income Scheme, if approved as part of the Finance Bill, would waive penalties for past tax evaders.

Chidambaram rejected calls from some lawmakers that he should maintain the peak personal income tax rate at 40 percent instead of cutting it to 30, and said India planned to cut the rate further to match fast-growing Asian economies.
"I am unable to accept this, because I believe that India's tax rates should be competitive and should encourage capital formation," he said.

Chidambaram said the investment climate in the country was expected to improve substantially following a recent fall in interest rates. The prrime lending rate at most banks has come down to about 14 percent compared with 18 percent two years ago, he said.
